newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch shares closed more than two percent down on Monday, reversing an earlier comeback from the day's lows as Wall Street stayed in negative territory.
The AEX blue chip index ended the day 23.09 points down at 973.07, off a session low of 971.53 established at opening.
An initial comeback on the back of a firming dollar reversed in the last half-hour of trade as Wall Street failed to climb into the black by the Amsterdam close.
Dealers said the opening fall in the index had been "exaggerated" as private investors cashed in their gains in the wake of Friday's Wall Street slide.

"The private investor sell-off was worsened by reports in some Dutch newspapers the share rally is over," one dealer said. "It was an over-reaction -- an exaggeration -- and the market later came back."
But while the firming dollar and recovering U.S. Treasuries looked to have restored confidence at midsession, the index later fell back once more to just above its opening level.
Dealers said overall volumes had been slow to moderate, with most institutionals staying sidelined ahead of a welter of U.S. macro-economic data due out later this week.
A lack of Dutch corporate news had also contributed to the lacklustre tone, with Friday's upcoming August expiry on the European Options Exchange having little impact on trade, dealers said.
Traders noted brisk trade in index-heavy financials as profit-takers stepped in on Friday's Treasury jitters.
"(Guilder) bonds are firmer and Treasuries are coming back (up), but last week's nerves have made players cash in their not inconsiderable gains," one said.
ABN AMRO lost 2.20 guilders to close at 48.30, while ING finished down 2.70 guilders at 98.80.
By contrast, chemicals group DSM added 1.30 guilders to close at 211.80 on demand from bargain-hunters.
Publisher Elsevier also spent much of the day in positive ground, buoyed by buying on dips after its recent fall. However, it ended the day down 0.10 at 32.80.
Wolters Kluwer, advised as an alternative buy by several analysts in the wake of Elsevier's disappointing first-half results, ended firmly up at 285.50, a gain of 3.50 .
Also higher was T.V. producer Endemol, which gained 1.10 guilders to 52.90 on news it had clinched a three-year deal with German commercial broadcaster RTL.
